title: The Book Store schema
idea: A schema file declares each table and its columns in JavaScript. Queries and `drizzle-kit` both read it, so every table has one definition.

analogy.text: A blueprint and a building. The schema file is the plan, the Postgres table is the building, and `drizzle-kit` is the crew that makes them match.
analogy.breaks: Tables hold data, so changing a built table is riskier than redrawing a plan.

points: `pgTable('books', {…})` declares a table: its SQL name, then one entry per column.
`serial()` auto-numbers ids, `text()` holds strings, `integer()` holds whole numbers.
`.primaryKey()` marks the unique id; `.notNull()` makes Postgres reject missing values.
`text('title')` names the Postgres column; the object key names the JavaScript field.

edges.label: read by
edges.caption: `schema.js` declares `books` once. `drizzle-kit push` reads it and compares it with the database.

edges.label: creates
edges.caption: It sends the SQL that makes the real `books` table match the schema.

edges.label: imported by
edges.caption: Your queries import the same `books` object, so `books.title` names a real column.

edges.label: reads rows
edges.caption: A query runs against the table and returns rows as plain objects.

code.title: src/db/schema.js
code.caption: The whole Book Store schema: one table, four columns. Step through it.

walk.text: Import the table builder and three column types from Drizzle's Postgres module.
`pgTable` takes the SQL table name, then an object of columns. `export` shares `books`.
`serial` numbers rows automatically; `primaryKey()` makes `id` each row's unique identifier.
`notNull()` makes Postgres reject a book without a title or an author.

code.title: Use the schema
code.caption: Imports `books` from `schema.js`, seeds the three Book Store rows and reads them back. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: Import `books` from the schema file: the same object every query uses.
`db` as in the last lesson, built from `DATABASE_URL`.
`drizzle-kit` is not run here, so raw SQL creates the table. It matches `schema.js`.
`insert().values()` takes objects keyed by the schema's field names, one per row.
`select().from(books)` returns rows as objects with those keys. `orderBy` fixes the order.
Close the pool so the script can exit.

pitfalls: Editing `schema.js` does not change Postgres: apply it, for example with `drizzle-kit push`.
If `schema.js` names a column the table lacks, queries fail: the column does not exist.
Export every table from the schema file, or `drizzle-kit` will not see it.

quiz.why: `year` has no `.notNull()`, so Postgres stores `null` when the insert leaves it out.

takeaway: Define a table once in `schema.js`; the database follows only when you apply it.
